Hi Laura — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments; helpful context. Short answer: we distinguish between (A) transactional billing artifacts (invoices, aggregated usage ledgers required for accounting) and (B) user-level content/interaction data covered by DSRs. For most DSRs we will remove or anonymize account-level identifiers from analytical traces and user-generated content as requested, but we retain a minimal set of billing evidence that is legally required for accounting and tax purposes.

CC'ing Neha (Finance) and Marissa (Legal) to give the canonical retention window and any required wording you can use in control docs. If you need a formal attestation letter for auditors, we can prepare that but will need GreenLeaf's exact retention requirements and jurisdiction.

Proposed next step: Neha can confirm retention periods and whether we can export an invoice-only archive with customer-identifying fields masked except for the legal name/invoice number. Marissa, please advise on any legal constraints on masking vs full preservation.

Hi all — quick finance perspective.

1) Retention windows: Redwood maintains invoice records and billing ledgers for seven (7) years by default to satisfy tax and audit requirements in our primary US jurisdiction. That includes: generated PDF invoices, per-invoice line-item usage summaries (aggregated by billing period), and our internal ledger entries.

2) DSR interplay: When a DSR requests erasure of user-level content or interaction traces, we perform the erasure on production/analytics stores and anonymize identifiable user metadata in aggregated datasets. However, the billing artifacts described above are exempted from full deletion when retention is legally required. We can, upon request, generate an invoice-only archive that omits sensitive behavioral logs and only includes the minimum identifying fields required for accounting (legal entity name, invoice number, billing address, invoice date, and aggregated usage totals).

3) Masking options: For customers who want the tightest privacy posture, we can mask internal customer IDs and replace them with a one-way hashed token in archived CSVs. The hash is not reversible by our standard ops team and can be provided to authorized auditors under an NDA/attestation if needed.

4) Audit attestation and format: We can provide PDF invoices (unchanged), a CSV ledger, and a signed letter confirming retention policy. Attached an example invoice for the same billing period (redwood-invoice-2026-06.pdf) — this is what auditors typically accept.

If GreenLeaf needs a custom retention exception (shorter or longer than 7 years), we can discuss via contract amendment. Marissa, please add if there are legal nuances for healthcare customers or cross-border data flows.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Head of Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Laura — quick legal note to make this board-ready for procurement controls:

- We confirm Redwood will retain accounting/billing records for seven years in the US, and that such retention is a legal/accounting exception to customer-directed erasure. The preserved set is limited to invoices, billing-ledger entries, payment receipts, and aggregated usage summaries needed for reconciliation.

- We will not preserve full user interaction logs, transcripts, or raw request payloads beyond their standard observability retention windows (these are subject to erasure/anonymization under a DSR).

- For healthcare customers: we handle PHI according to the contract and any applicable BAAs; retention of invoices does not imply retention of PHI in billing artifacts — billing artifacts will only include necessarily minimal billing identifiers.

Action items: Priya — I'll draft a short two-paragraph attestation you can send to GreenLeaf summarizing the points above. Neha — confirm whether the invoice-only archive can be produced as a zipped CSV + PDF bundle (with masked internal IDs) and provide an estimated delivery SLT (we typically do these in 3 business days).

Marissa Cole
